body: A New York Supreme Court judge has ordered a foreclosure auction of 500 and 512 Seventh Avenue, two Midtown office buildings, to satisfy a $356 million debt, The Real Deal reported on Aug. 24, 2026. According to court documents cited by the publication, the borrower agreed not to oppose the lender's foreclosure motion. The lender filed its foreclosure suit in July 2025.

The borrower, 500-512 Seventh Avenue Limited Partnership, is a partnership of brothers Meyer and Joseph Chetrit, Joseph Moinian and Edward Minskoff. It bought the leasehold for $140 million in 1999 and borrowed $375 million against the buildings in 2018. The loan also covers 228 West 38th Street. No. 512 is a 45-story tower with 544,300 rentable square feet, and No. 500 is an 18-story building with 676,500 rentable square feet. The Chetrit Group has its offices in No. 512.

The lender's case centers on that office lease. It says the Chetrit Group ran up more than $1 million in unpaid rent, and an attorney for the lender told the court the failure was "evidence of self-dealing or, at a minimum, severe negligence and mismanagement," given that the guarantor is an insider of the borrower. In a deposition this spring, Meyer Chetrit said the Chetrit Group held a 56 percent stake and had never paid the $42,000 rent on its offices in the "four or five" years it had been there, The Real Deal reported. The lender had earlier accused the borrower of moving $1 million in tenant security deposits to outside funds, including $300,000 to other Chetrit Group projects or associates, and of missing monthly payments.

Representatives for the Chetrits, Moinian and Minskoff did not immediately respond to The Real Deal's request for comment. Asked in the deposition where the foreclosure stood, Meyer Chetrit answered: "About to lose it already."

timeline.label: 500-512 Seventh Avenue Limited Partnership buys the leasehold for $140M
Borrower takes out a $375M loan against the buildings
Lender files foreclosure suit in New York Supreme Court
Judge orders a foreclosure sale to satisfy a $356M debt; borrower did not oppose
